sentences.text: Idiacanthus is a genus of barbeled dragonfishes whose larvae exhibit the Stylophthalmine trait, a name derived from Greek words meaning 'own' and 'spine' or 'thorn'.

Three species are recognized in this group: Idiacanthus antrostomus, known as the Pacific black dragon; Idiacanthus atlanticus, the Atlantic black dragon; and Idiacanthus fasciola, the common black dragon.

Modern members belong to the family Stomiidae, subfamily Idiacanthinae, order Stomiiformes, and class Actinopterygii, while a fossil genus named Idiacanthus by Gunnell in 1933 is classified under Chondrichthyes and lived from the Moscovian to Kasimovian periods.
Known as devil fish or black dragons, these marine fish of the stomiid family are distributed in the abyssal waters of all oceans and can reach a maximum length between 38 and 53 cm.
Females can grow up to 40 cm in length with black skin, whereas males reach a maximum of 5 cm and are dark brown.
Male Idiacanthus lack teeth, a chin barbel, and a functioning gut.
A fertile female Idiacanthus fasciola can hold approximately 14,000 eggs.
These fish possess a strip of chevron-shaped luminescent tissue along their dorsal and ventral sides that glows yellow or blue-green when stimulated, but the light lasts only a few seconds.
The premaxilla, maxilla, and mandible teeth of Idiacanthidae are almost all capable of being depressed, a feature relevant to their diet.
Idiacanthidae have pectoral fins in their larval stage but lose them in adulthood, indicating a change in locomotion.

Both male and female Idiacanthus have small photophores spread throughout their bodies, and studies by William T. O'Day in 1973 showed that Idiacanthus luminescent tissue can be stimulated by adrenaline injection, topical application, seawater solutions with adrenaline, or tactile touch.

Members of the genus Idiacanthus live in the mesopelagic and bathypelagic zones, with Idiacanthus fasciola widely distributed in the North and South Atlantic, the Indo-Pacific, and other areas, while Idiacanthus antrostomus is mainly found in the Eastern Pacific.
